review_reference: UNSIGNED DRAFT: awaits the owner's signature of 0160 and 0161 and of runtime-grants.sql at the sha256s in files (numbers provisional, given at integration in release order: #258, 7168672285; the order is now fixed as 0154, Appointments, Billing, Emergency, one department per release, so at integration these files become 0155 and 0156 after 0154, their sha256s change again, and this declaration is re-made and signed at the new numbers). APPT-1 Appointments with check-in to the waiting list (Release D, the department sprint the owner approved on 25 November 2026; hid-system#335), built at the recommended option of each open question, not yet answered by the owner: Q-APPT-1 A (check-in from an appointment opens the waiting-list row in the same transaction), Q-APPT-2 A (timed bookings with a server clash check, the clinician optional), Q-APPT-3 A (inbox, web push, email and the printable call list; SMS built but switched off), Q-APPT-4 A (staff book; the portal is read only), Q-APPT-5 A (who books), Q-APPT-6 A (an appointment is a check-in-only basis on its own day; Rahman's database check of 25 November answered A) and Q-APPT-7 A (the call list shows only the phone this facility recorded). ehr-api's and identity-api's APPOINTMENTS_ENABLED stay off in production until the clinical lead's checklist and the owner's go-live. Rahman's final database check of 63312e5f (#335, 25 November 20:51 UTC) found nothing blocking; this head carries his four should-fix points and the nits, as the coordinator decided on #258 (7174680244): 0160 takes identity.sealed_demo_members and identity.sealed_qa_members ACCESS SHARE NOWAIT up front (statement, both busy refusals, header, the suite's declared locks); runtime-grants.sql revokes ehr.appointment_events_sequence_no_seq from hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, and 0160 post-checks that the sequences its tables own carry no grant beyond the owner; post-checks in 0148's and 0152's form (the six tables and 27 functions owned by the owner of 0135's functions, row-level security enabled and not forced with no policy, the triggers by tgtype, tgqual, tgattr, tgnargs, tgfoid and tgenabled, and 0161 re-checks the control_key CHECK it rewrites); tolerant preconditions (the codes 0001-0151 give receptionist, doctor, clinician and nurse required as a subset, with no appointment code yet; a basis CHECK with other lanes' values after search and own_facility, rebuilt as search, own_facility, appointment and then those values); a BEFORE TRUNCATE guard on the appointment history; the not-forced row-level security stated as an exception in both headers; the runbook note that a role bootstrap after 0160 and 0161 uses the integration's runtime-grants.sql before the new images ship (docs/MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md, Appointments). It also carries the three findings independent reviewers confirmed on 7a3ad90d: the reminder SMS now follows the email's patient rule (an active patient with notices on, 0063), both when the sweep queues it and when identity.appointment_sms_claim claims it, which closes a row that fails the rule unsent (failed, PATIENT_NOT_REACHABLE) as it closes one whose appointment is no longer booked, so a patient who has died, is inactive, merged or deleted, or has turned notices off gets no SMS, as the inbox and email paths already did (notices off is honoured as for the email; the DPO may decide otherwise before the control is switched on, and the status check stays either way); 0160 no longer requires 0149's marker (ehr.catalog_versions), whose objects it does not use (markers only for earlier files whose objects a file uses, #258 7168672285), so its markers are 0145's and 0150's; and the appointments suite books 'tomorrow' at 10:00 Lagos tomorrow and 'today' at a step that cannot leave today (the notices suite's one booking for today likewise), so neither suite fails late in the evening or just after midnight. Rahman's own final check, round 2, of d7511876 (#335, 26 November 2026 03:55 UTC, 7182156812) found nothing blocking and two should-fix items; this head carries both, with his nits, since the files are re-hashed anyway: (1) identity.appointment_sms_claim always answers a lease, as the email claim does: it leases only rows it can return (the appointment still booked, reminded by the sweep since its last move and starting within 24 hours; the patient active with notices on; the facility contact unerased; attempts left), taking the facility name, start time and phone from the rows it leased, and closes a row that can never be sent, at any hour (failed: APPOINTMENT_NOT_BOOKED, APPOINTMENT_STARTED, PATIENT_NOT_REACHABLE, CONTACT_ERASED after 0114's erasure or an account deletion, ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED after 5 attempts and a lapsed lease); the sweep writes the SMS row first, names sms among the audited channels only when it wrote the row, takes an unsent SMS whose lease has lapsed back into the queue, and leaves an appointment whose unsent SMS is under a live lease for its next run (no notice, no reminder_sent_at, no audit row yet), so a booking moved while its SMS is sent gets the new time once the lease is answered; (2) the notices suite replaces the sweep's and the claim's clock line inside its own rolled-back transaction (owner, grants, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path kept, the real guards checked at their edges), so every reminder and SMS case runs at any hour. Nits: the claim leases only between 07:00 and 21:00 Lagos, never after the start, and never at once for an unsent SMS kept by a move days ahead; the SMS outbox records the lease's sender (claimed_by), identity.appointment_sms_claim(text, integer) and identity.appointment_sms_record(uuid, text, text, text) take it, and the record answers sent, pending, failed or stale (another sender's or a lapsed-and-requeued lease: stale, nothing recorded, where it raised 55000) and refuses a null outcome; 0160 accepts only 'emergency' after 0135's two basis values; "already applied" needs every object of each file (0160: the four tables, the 18 functions by signature, exactly the two codes and the seven role rows by role and code; 0161: the two tables, the nine functions, the CHECK and the trigger), and any part is a half state; the appointments-migrations suite shows every declared lock taken in the file's NOWAIT lock step at exactly its declared mode, from a second session before this transaction locks anything (so the setup cannot hide one); the EXECUTE post-checks of both files are in 0148's form (each runtime that exists holds EXECUTE on its own functions, never with grant option; no other role holds any); the comment on ehr.appointment_sms_outbox states the current rule. From an independent review stopped before verification, verified and fixed here: identity.appointment_call_list showed deceased, merged and inactive patients with the facility-recorded phone, and now lists only active patients (the check-in and the other reminder channels refuse them); 0161's post-checks now check the notice trigger's function and the notice helper by body, neither SECURITY DEFINER, with the fixed search_path (as 0152 and 0160); the runbook states the fixed release order. From a second independent review of ae6f6560, four findings, each verified and fixed here: (1) identity.appointment_sms_claim answered the phone saved when the SMS was queued even after the desk recorded a newer one (0130's link_existing approval adds one); it now answers the phone as the facility records it when the row is leased, the newest unerased phone of the patient at that facility, as the sweep and the call list take it, and the lease records that contact, so CONTACT_ERASED now means that no unerased phone of the patient at the facility is left; (2) should-fix: the sweep took a lapsed lease back into the queue whatever its attempts, so a booking moved after five unanswered leases had its spent SMS revived at 5 attempts and sms audited, and the claim then closed it unsent (the symptom of Rahman's round-2 item 1, in the exhausted-lease path); the sweep now takes a lapsed lease back only while it has attempts left and otherwise leaves the appointment for its next run (no notice, no reminder_sent_at, no audit row), the claim closes the spent SMS (ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED) and the next sweep queues a new one with the new time; (3) identity.appointment_email_claim left a row whose 5 attempts were spent and whose last lease had lapsed claimed for good; it now closes such a row as failed (attempts_exhausted, finished), as the SMS claim does, while a row without a verified recipient is still closed as skipped; (4) 0160's header and the contract's database-release paragraph state the fixed release order (one department per release: 0154, Appointments, Billing, Emergency; numbers closed up at integration), as the runbook does. The notices suite has a case for each of (1)-(3). runtime-grants.sql is Release E's signed file (49b378f5..., signed 25 November 2026 with 0152 and 0153) byte for byte followed by the Appointments block, whose only change since d7511876 is the two SMS signatures (unchanged since ae6f6560). identity-api's SMS sender passes its worker id to the claim and the record and counts the record's answer. Releases after 0001-0153 (Release E, live since 25 November 2026 17:04 UTC at 0cfddcc9), after 0154 in the fixed order; it also applies before or after Emergency (0168-0169). Billing's 0162 (6b253568) refuses after Appointments on its own role pin, which is that lane's to fix (Rahman, round 2). Rahman's re-check and the owner's signature are pending.
evidence: On throwaway PostgreSQL 16 databases (Docker, image hid-pg16-vector:local, with pgvector) with fictional data only. This head (the files at the sha256s in files; 0160 differs from ae6f6560's only in its header comment, 0161 in the SMS claim's phone lookup and closing pass, the sweep's revive condition, the email claim's closing pass and comments; runtime-grants.sql is unchanged): the base is 0001-0153 (live 0cfddcc9's files, by git archive) built by the repo runner as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds; 154 recorded), then Release E's runtime-grants.sql (49b378f5...) as the bootstrap runs it; on copies of it, once without staff and once with fictional staff (an active receptionist, doctor, clinician, nurse and lab member at one real facility): plan 2 pending at the sha256s in files, dry run rolled back, apply, plan 0 pending, then this runtime-grants.sql (25b861e6...). Suites, each on both copies: appointments 128 of 128, appointment-notices 121 of 121 and appointments-migrations 100 of 100 at 14:50 Lagos on 26 November, and again (with the staff) at 01:55 Lagos (27 November) on a server whose wall clock was moved forward for the test (a test-only LD_PRELOAD clock shift in the throwaway container). The six new notices cases, run against ae6f6560's 0160 and 0161 (f850d3af..., a9703e87...) on a copy of the same base: exactly four checks fail, one per finding: the claim answered the queued phone ('Reminder Clinic A:0202:v1:01 | claimed:02' where A's call list showed '0505:13'); after five lapsed leases and a move the sweep answered 1, audited sms and left the spent row 'pending:-:5', the claim then closed it and the next sweep answered 0, so the moved booking got no SMS; and the email row with 5 attempts and a lapsed lease stayed 'claimed:5:-:unfinished'. Every build by the repo runner as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, as the upgrade rehearsal runs it); the role bootstrap and the suites run by the cluster superuser. The base: 0001-0153 (live 0cfddcc9's files, compared byte for byte) with Release E's runtime-grants.sql (49b378f5...), plus fictional staff (an active receptionist, doctor, clinician, nurse and lab member at one real facility), so 0160's closing count reaches rows as it does on production. Rahman's points (earlier round, 7a3ad90d): before them, 63312e5f's 0160 and 0161 on that base with runtime-grants.sql 732f7248...: appointments-migrations failed case 4h with 'identity.sealed_demo_members AccessShareLock, identity.sealed_qa_members AccessShareLock'; a dry run while another session held identity.sealed_qa_members failed after 5 s with 'canceling statement due to lock timeout', which the runner does not retry; after the bootstrap the history's sequence carried USAGE and SELECT for hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; and 0160 refused after Billing's 0162-0167 and after Emergency's 0168-0169 (the role table). After them: the same dry run gave 0160's busy refusal, was retried and succeeded; after the bootstrap the sequence carries no grant but its owner's (checked again on this head). The reviewers' findings on 7a3ad90d: with its 0160 (8b553f31...) and 0161 (08238706...) on a copy of the base, this head's appointment-notices suite failed its four new SMS cases: with appointment_sms_reminders_enabled on, the sweep queued an SMS for a deceased patient (channels ["sms"]) and for an active patient with notices off (["inbox", "email", "sms"]), and identity.appointment_sms_claim, as the Identity runtime, handed out the queued SMS with the facility name and the phone ciphertext in both cases (the sweep cases run with the 07:00-21:00 Lagos guard switched off by create or replace inside the rolled-back run, owner and grants kept, since the runs were at about 23:15 Lagos); 7a3ad90d's appointments suite failed '6 tomorrow's list at A, booked only' and '6 tomorrow, the clinic's' at 23:16 Lagos, as the reviewers reported. With d7511876 (the same 0160, 0161 and runtime-grants.sql as this head, byte for byte) on a copy of the same base: plan 2 pending at the sha256s in files, dry run rolled back, apply, plan 0 pending; then this runtime-grants.sql. A first attempt under heavy machine load stopped in the clean install's patient-self suite ('expired self context retained clinical access': the rehearsal sends that suite as one query, so statement_timestamp() is its start and a run slower than a second keeps the context it means to expire), unrelated to this release; the re-run passed. Re-running Release E's runtime-grants.sql after 0160 and 0161 takes the EHR and Identity runtimes' EXECUTE on the appointment functions away and gives the sequence back (hence the runbook note). Release tests 123 of 126: 45, 53 and 100 fail only with 'missing migration prefix' (the provisional numbering gap 0154-0159), and 67 passes; verify-migration-ledger accepts 0161 (156 files); build gates 70; scripts/tests 82 and 1 skipped; ehr-api jest 23 (appointments and the 0136 count spec); identity-api jest 485 (the specs that read every migration, and appointments). Round 2 (the second independent review, of d7511876: two findings, both in the suites; 0160, 0161 and runtime-grants.sql unchanged, at the same sha256s): the appointments-migrations suite's new case 1c3 holds identity.sealed_demo_members in ACCESS EXCLUSIVE from another session, as 1c2 holds identity.sealed_qa_members, and expects 0160's busy refusal with nothing applied, so both sealed-member tables are shown taken NOWAIT up front; with a scratch copy of 0160 that leaves identity.sealed_demo_members out of its lock step, the suite fails at 1c3 (got '55000 0160: already applied'). The appointment-notices suite no longer skips the sweep's cases outside 07:00-21:00 Lagos: 0161's own sweep runs at the suite's hour and is undone (the two due reminders between 07:00 and 21:00 Lagos, none outside); then, inside the rolled-back run only, a copy of the sweep whose one change is that the suite sets its Lagos hour (create or replace; the suite checks that 0161's clock line was found once and that the owner, grants, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path are kept) checks 0161's guard at 06, 07, 20 and 21 and runs every other sweep case, the SMS patient-rule ones included, at noon Lagos.
